channel.title: BMW recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: BMW M550i Driveshaft Connection May Fail
item.description: On certain BMW vehicles including the M550i xDrive, the connection between the driveshaft and the rear differential can become damaged. This can cause a loss of power to the rear wheels while driving, or it can lead to the vehicle rolling away on its own if the parking brake isn't set. A sudden loss of power increases the risk of a crash, and an unexpected rollaway increases the risk of a crash or injury.

item.title: BMW X3 Steering Spindle May Be Loose
item.description: On certain BMW X3 vehicles, the steering spindle—the part that connects the steering wheel to the steering column—may not have been properly attached. This is a problem with the physical connection inside the steering system, between the steering wheel and the column beneath it. If this connection is not secure, the way the vehicle steers could be affected.

item.title: BMW S 1000 RR Ignition Lock May Fail
item.description: On some BMW S 1000 RR motorcycles, vibration can cause a part inside the ignition lock to fail. This can knock out the instrument display, rear lighting, and other systems like ABS, or cause the engine to stall while you're riding. BMW is still developing a repair. In the meantime, the company is mailing letters to let owners know about this safety risk.

item.title: BMW, Mini Integrated Brake System May Malfunction
item.description: The integrated brake system in these vehicles may malfunction. This can cause a loss of power brake assist, which affects how the brakes work. It can also cause the Antilock Brake System and the Dynamic Stability Control system to stop functioning properly. To fix this, the integrated brake system will be inspected and, if necessary, replaced, free of charge for owners.

item.title: BMW K 1600 Motorcycles Reverse Gear Overheating Risk
item.description: On these motorcycles, a seal on the reverse gear control unit can deteriorate over time and let moisture get inside the unit. If moisture gets in, the control unit can overheat. Dealers will replace the reverse gear control unit at no charge, and a follow-up letter will be sent once the final remedy is ready.

item.title: BMW, Toyota Supra: Engine Starter May Catch Fire
item.description: On affected vehicles, the engine starter may overheat and catch fire due to wear on an internal component.

item.title: BMW i4 Loose Battery Cable Risks Fire
item.description: BMW is recalling one 2025 i4 eDrive40 vehicle because the connection between the positive battery cable and the rear power distributor may come loose over time.

item.title: BMW X3 Steering Wheel May Move Unexpectedly
item.description: Certain 2025 and 2026 BMW X3 vehicles may experience unexpected movement of the steering wheel while the vehicle is stationary, meaning it isn't being driven at that moment. The steering wheel can rotate on its own, without the driver turning it, even though no one is actively steering the vehicle.

item.title: BMW R 1300 RT Motorcycles May Lose Drive Power
item.description: BMW is recalling certain 2026 R 1300 RT motorcycles because the cardan shaft may not have been hardened enough. This can allow the universal joint to slip within the shaft, causing a loss of drive power while riding.

item.title: BMW X5, X6, X7 Starter May Overheat
item.description: After repeated starting attempts, the starter motor in these vehicles may overheat because of an electrical overload. An overheated starter sitting in the engine compartment can get hot enough to ignite nearby material that catches fire easily.

item.title: BMW and Toyota Supra Starter Relay Fire Risk
item.description: Certain BMW X3, X4, Z4, and Toyota Supra vehicles have an engine starter relay that can corrode over time. Once corroded, the relay may overheat and short circuit. This electrical problem can increase the risk of a fire, whether the vehicle is being driven or is already parked.

item.title: BMW X1, X2, Mini Countryman Seat Belt Retractor Damage
item.description: In certain BMW X1, X2, and Mini Countryman S ALL4 vehicles, the torsion bar inside both front seat belt retractors may have been damaged during manufacturing.

item.title: BMW R 1300 GS, S 1000 RR eCall Disabled
item.description: These motorcycles can come equipped with an optional emergency call system, a feature designed to automatically reach out for help if you're in a crash. A software programming error may have caused this system to be turned off. When that happens, the emergency call feature will not work the way it's meant to when it's needed most, since it has already been deactivated by the error.

item.title: BMW Electric Models May Lose Drive Power
item.description: Certain BMW i4, i5, i7, and iX electric vehicles have a software issue in the electric drive motor. This software may shut down the vehicle's high-voltage system, which causes a sudden loss of drive power while you're driving. BMW will fix this with a software update, either sent over-the-air or done by a dealer, at no cost to you. Owner notification letters have been mailed to affected drivers.

item.title: BMW i4 and iX: Battery Module Failure Risk
item.description: Some high-voltage battery cell modules were not put together correctly, which can put stress on the module frame. Over time, this may cause a battery module to fail. BMW has already mailed letters warning owners about this risk, and will send another notice once dealers can begin replacing the affected battery modules for free.

item.title: BMW X3 Front Brake Discs Damaged in Transport
item.description: The front brake discs on affected vehicles may have been damaged during transport, before they were ever installed on the vehicle.

item.title: BMW 430i, X3 Starter Connection May Loosen
item.description: The electrical connection between the starter-generator and the battery in your vehicle may come loose. If this happens while you're driving, your engine could stall. The wiring involved in this connection may also overheat. Dealers will inspect the starter-generator and battery cable and replace them if necessary, free of charge. BMW has already mailed an interim letter about this, and a second letter will follow once the full repair is ready.

item.title: BMW M 1000 Motorcycles Steering Can Suddenly Stiffen
item.description: On these motorcycles, the steering damper may have a valve pin that is loose inside its housing instead of properly secured. When the pin is loose, it can cause the amount of effort needed to turn the handlebars to increase suddenly while you are riding. This unexpected change in steering effort can make the motorcycle harder to keep under control.

item.title: BMW X3 Rear Brake Hoses May Leak, Cut Braking
item.description: On some BMW X3 vehicles, the rear brake hoses may develop a leak. If that happens, the vehicle can lose rear brake function, and it can also lose the Antilock Brake System and Dynamic Stability Control, systems that help keep the vehicle stable.

item.title: BMW X3 Battery Cable May Overheat
item.description: On some 2025 BMW X3 30 xDrive vehicles, the connection between the positive battery cable and the starter-generator may not have been tightened properly, which can cause it to overheat.

item.title: BMW X3 rear door locks may open too easily
item.description: Certain BMW X3 vehicles have door locking modules on the second-row side doors that may not work correctly. Normally, unlocking and opening a rear door takes separate steps. But with this problem, those doors could be unlocked and opened at the same time with just one motion, meaning a single accidental movement could open the door instead of just unlocking it.

item.title: BMW X3 Front Left Wheel Bearing May Crack
item.description: The swivel bearing at the front left wheel may crack. If it does, it can cause the driver to lose handling and control of the vehicle.

item.title: BMW X4 Roof Crack May Damage Head Air Bag
item.description: The roof frame near the head air bag on the inner-left side may have a crack. If it does, the crack can damage the head air bag as it deploys, so it may not protect the occupant properly in a crash.

item.title: BMW X3 Side Curtain Airbag May Not Deploy Right
item.description: On some 2025 BMW X3 30 xDrive vehicles, the gas generator inside the right-side head curtain airbag may have been put together incorrectly during assembly. This could cause the airbag to deploy late or not work the way it's supposed to in a crash. Dealers will inspect the airbag and replace it if needed, free of charge. None of these vehicles have been sold yet.

item.title: BMW X1 B-Pillar May Lack Crash Strength
item.description: On certain BMW X1 xDrive28i and X1 M35i vehicles, the reinforcement plates in the left and right B-Pillars may have been manufactured with insufficient structural strength. Because these pillars may not be as strong as they should be, they may not properly protect passengers if the vehicle is ever in a crash. This increases the risk of injury to people riding inside the vehicle if a crash happens.

item.title: BMW X3 Passenger Air Bag May Not Inflate
item.description: Some new X3 SUVs may have a front passenger air bag with damaged fabric. The damage is believed to have happened while the air bag was being shipped between suppliers before it was installed in the vehicle. If the fabric is damaged, the air bag may not inflate the way it's supposed to in a crash. That means it may not protect the front passenger as intended, raising the risk of injury if a crash occurs. None of the affected vehicles have been sold yet.

item.title: BMW X3 rear cargo rail can detach in crash
item.description: BMW is recalling certain X3 models. The bracket that holds the cargo rail in the rear of the vehicle can be damaged in a rear-end crash, and the rail can come loose and separate from the vehicle. Dealers will replace the bolts that hold the rear cargo rail in place, free of charge. Vehicles covered by this recall had work done for this same problem under an earlier recall, and they still need the new repair.

item.title: BMW Brake System May Lose Power Assist
item.description: Certain BMW models with an integrated brake system may have the system malfunction. This can cause a loss of power assist for the brakes, meaning it takes more pedal effort and distance to stop the vehicle. The malfunction can also stop the Antilock Brake System and Dynamic Stability Control from working properly, which can affect the driver's ability to keep control of the vehicle.

item.title: BMW R18 Reverse Gear Control Unit May Overheat
item.description: On some BMW R18 motorcycles, the seal on the reverse gear control unit may deteriorate over time, allowing moisture to get inside the unit. Once moisture gets inside, it can cause the control unit to overheat. This overheating is the safety problem this recall is meant to fix.

item.title: BMW and MINI Brake System Weld May Fail
item.description: The welds inside the servomotor of the integrated brake control module may break. If this happens, the vehicle can lose power assist for the brakes and lose function in the rear brakes. The antilock brake system and the dynamic stability control system may also stop working properly. To fix the problem, BMW dealers will replace the entire integrated brake system with a new one.

item.title: BMW X4, X5 Water Pump Connector May Short
item.description: An electrical connector on the engine's water pump was not properly sealed, so it can be exposed to water. If water reaches it, the connector can short circuit.

item.title: BMW Starter Motor Overheating May Cause Engine Fire
item.description: If the starter motor fails, repeated attempts to start the vehicle can cause the starter motor to overheat from an electrical overload. This affects certain BMW M340i, X5, X6, and X7 vehicles, among other models. Dealers will update the vehicle software, free of charge.

item.title: BMW R 1300 GS Starter Relay May Overheat
item.description: BMW is recalling certain R 1300 GS motorcycles because the housing for the starter motor relay may have been made incorrectly. This can damage the relay and cause it to overheat.

item.title: BMW X3 Interior Cargo Rail May Come Loose
item.description: BMW is recalling certain X3 vehicles, including the sDrive30i, xDrive30i, M40i and X3 M. The attachment that holds the interior cargo rail in place can be damaged if the vehicle is struck from behind, and the cargo rail can then come loose inside the vehicle. Dealers will replace the bolts that fasten the rear cargo rail at no cost. Owners have been sent notification letters about this repair.

item.title: BMW SUVs May Have Seat Belt Sensor Defect
item.description: Certain BMW X5, X6, X7, XM, and Alpina XB7 vehicles have a seat belt system that may wrongly detect a passenger as buckled in when they are not. This can keep the seat belt warning light from turning on, and it may also keep the airbag system from deploying the way it is supposed to in a crash. Dealers will inspect the front seat lower seat belts and replace them if necessary.

item.title: BMW X5 Tire Placard Lists Wrong Information
item.description: The tire information placard on these vehicles may show the wrong tire size and tire pressure. Because the numbers printed on it are incorrect, the placard does not give accurate information about which tires should be used or how much air should be in them. This means the information a driver would see on that label may not match what the vehicle actually needs.

item.title: BMW Motorcycle Front Strut Failure Risk
item.description: BMW is recalling certain R 1250RT, K 1600GT, K 1600GTL, and K 1600B motorcycles because the front spring strut may contain an incorrectly manufactured proportional valve. This valve can loosen, and when it does, the strut itself can fail. If the strut fails, the motorcycle can become unstable while it is being ridden, affecting how well the rider can keep the motorcycle steady and balanced.

item.title: BMW XM Tailgate Panel May Detach From Vehicle
item.description: Some 2024 BMW XM vehicles have a tailgate panel that may detach from the mounting structure. This can happen because of improper adhesive bonding that occurred during manufacturing. A panel that detaches from the vehicle can fall onto the road and become a hazard for other drivers. This is a road hazard that increases the chance of a crash for the vehicle or others nearby.

item.title: BMW i5 High-Voltage Battery May Overheat
item.description: The high-voltage battery module in these vehicles may not have enough weld seams, or the welds inside it may be incomplete. This is a manufacturing issue with the battery itself. Because of the weak welds, the battery module can overheat. An overheated high-voltage battery raises the risk that a fire could start in the vehicle. The battery module will need to be inspected and replaced to fix this problem.

item.title: BMW X5, X7 Instrument Panel Airbag Deployment Issue
item.description: On some 2024 X5 and X7 models, the instrument panel may not have been built correctly. Because of this, the panel could come apart when the airbag deploys, or the airbag itself may not deploy properly. Either problem could mean pieces of the panel strike someone inside the vehicle, or that an occupant isn't restrained as intended by the airbag during a crash.
